key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can learn interpretable corrections to a simple k-ε-b turbulence closure, improving Rayleigh-Taylor mixing predictions during the transition to turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This offers a path to more reliable RANS-based models for mixed-flow and stratified-flow applications where turbulence is underdeveloped and standard closures struggle.
method: Embed the k-ε-b model in a surrogate PINN to calibrate uncertain coefficients.
Learn corrective terms for structural model errors caused by missing physics.
Re-express the learned corrections as explicit analytical modifications using flow variables and indicators.
evidence_signal: The corrected model is validated against an extensive DNS database of Rayleigh-Taylor flows and shows improved mixing-layer growth predictions.
watch_item: The learned closure is tailored to the transitional Rayleigh-Taylor regime, so generalization to other flow classes or stronger extrapolation conditions may need additional validation.
paper_title: Learning Turbulence Closures with Physics-Informed Neural Networks for the Rayleigh-Taylor Transition to Turbulence
